label: <DEL> step, first token to copy is d/k/v/b/3/m/e/w
explanation: Almost only fires at the delimiter step (96% of activation mass; 12% of <DEL> steps are active). It never fires in the original phase and only rarely in the copy phase, mostly at recall_idx 1 when the token being output is one of the same favoured tokens. Within <DEL> steps, whether it fires depends on which token is about to be copied first (orig(0)): rate is d 11.7x, k 7.2x, v 6.7x, b 6.3x, 3 and m 4.8x, e and w about 4x. A second favoured token as orig(1) (d, v, k, 3, x, s, b, e) also raises the rate, and so do long sequences (L=8-9, plus L=3). The largest activations (top examples) are <DEL> steps in long sequences that start with d, b, v or k, often followed by another favoured token. It looks like a graded sum over the identities of the first one or two tokens to recall, and a single boolean only partly captures it: <DEL> & orig(0) in the set gives dev F1 0.49 / mass recall 0.84; adding orig(1)-in-set-or-L>=8 gives F1 0.57 / mass recall 0.72.
